Residents of a breezy beach community in California are up-in-arms over the fact that a gun store is opening next to one of the city's daycares.

Goodland Guns announced last month that it was moving next door to Here We Grow Early Learning Center in Goleta , a community of just over 30,000 people located just north of Santa Barbara, California.

On August 3, members of the community rallied in a parking lot adjacent to the daycare. Demonstrators gave statements opposing the opening of a gun store next door, according to SFGATE.

Dan Ashton, the owner of the gun store, and Goleta City Council members also attended the rally to address the concerns of the community members.

Ashton told SFGATE that the store is opening at the new spot despite the outcry. The grand opening is set for September 5.

Community members in Goleta, California are pushing back against a gun store that is opening next door to a daycare center ( AFP/Getty )

He told the paper if he could have it his way he'd stay at his current location in Old Town Goleta. He's been operating his gun store from that location for 11 years, but was recently told to vacate by his landlord so they could raise the rent on the property.

That left Ashton scrambling for a new home for his business.

“Finding a commercial location took three years of continuous searching, with regular communications with the city over the last 12 months,” he told SFGATE. “Due to Goleta’s rapid growth and the exodus of businesses from Santa Barbara, commercial and industrial spaces are incredibly scarce—especially for a highly regulated firearms retailer.”

He said he did not have "the luxury of waiting" for the perfect spot to open up.

“Although commercial rent increases in California are capped at 10% annually, this unfortunately seems to be a convenient workaround for building owners," he wrote to the paper. "Small businesses in California are being squeezed out by skyrocketing commercial rents, and this was the only viable location that accommodated the State’s strict operational requirements.”

Ashton said he thought he had some productive conversations with concerned residents at the rally, and said his goal is to be a good neighbor, wherever his shop is located.

“We want to be good neighbors, which is why we’ve proactively implemented feasible solutions in direct response to my neighbors’ input," he said.

That said, some residents of Goleta are still critical of a gun shop operating so close to a children's educational center. An online petition is collecting signatures from concerned residents in a big to prevent the gun shop from opening.

“Our children attend Ellwood Elementary, and live just down the street from this location, walking by it regularly,” a one of the petitioners wrote. “There must be a more appropriate place for this business to set up shop instead of within a high density, family oriented neighborhood adjacent to a wonderful preschool.”

The city's officials confirmed to SFGATE that they're aware of the issue and said they're working on solutions.

“We are going to bring some options back that could lead to a change in our zoning or an ordinance that would put potentially more restrictions where gun stores could be located,” Goleta City Manager Robert Nisbet told the outlet.

The gun store's location and relevant zoning issues will be on the schedule for the September 1 Goleta City Council meeting, Nisbet said.

He noted that even if the city cracks down on where gun stores can be located, it's not likely going to affect Ashton's gun store.

Ashton said he doesn't blame the city for his difficulties finding a viable spot to operate his business, but the state's strict laws regulation businesses like his.

The city was simply doing its job interpreting (although incorrectly at times) and enforcing the incredibly strict California Building Code (CBC) and California Fire Code (CFC)," he wrote. "The real issue is the crushing regulatory environment the State of California has created for small businesses. The state makes it nearly impossible to open, move, or survive.”

The Independent has requested comment from the daycare.

News.title: Russell takes Dutch GP sprint pole as Antonelli struggles to fifth
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for sprint qualifying for the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix from Zandvoort. This is the last time the race will be on the F1 calendar for the foreseeable future, having been reintroduced in 2021 after a 35-year absence. It will be a shame to see it leave again, but never rule out it coming back, especially with Max Verstappen signing a lengthy contract extension with Red Bull.

What of the competitive action this weekend? As it is a sprint weekend, there is not a lot of preparation time, with just one practice session before sprint qualifying. In that it was a fairly close fight at the top, and it was Kimi Antonelli, the championship leader, who was fastest of all. Behind him was the McLaren of Lando Norris who was 0.121sec adrift then George Russell, who will be looking to kickstart his title campaign here, a further 0.004sec behind him.

Then came the two Ferraris of Lewis Hamilton (0.190sec) and Charles Leclerc (0.289sec) before a fairly significant gap of 0.659sec to Oscar Piastri in sixth. Verstappen was down in 11th, nearly 1.4sec off Antonelli’s ultimate pace but 0.5sec or so ahead of new (and old) team-mate for the weekend, Liam Lawson.

It was a tricky session for the drivers, though, as it began damp on a showery and blustery day by the Dutch seaside. Several drivers ran wide and off the track, though they all avoided anything more serious than gravel rash. The rest of the day looks to be drier but there are still a few showers around and the wind is all over the place, as it often is here.

Sprint qualifying starts at 3.30pm BST and we will be here for all of the updates for the nearly hour-long session.

News.title: Root delivers perfect riposte to captaincy doubters as England hammer Pakistan
News.content:
There was no attempt to be a Ben Stokes tribute act by Joe Root, just a measured captaincy performance very much in his own undemonstrative style.

Root, ever the team man, pushed his bowlers forward to lead England off at the end, recognising the match-winners in a walkover against Pakistan, who were bowled out for 135 in under two sessions.

Victory by an innings and 103 runs inside three days marked a perfect return to the job and put the smile back on England faces for the first time in a long while. The chants of “F--- the ECB” from Trent Bridge, after the New Zealand regime-toppling loss, were replaced by the Yorkshire faithful’s “Roooot”.

There was plenty of scepticism around rebooting the Root captaincy, but he was the only realistic choice. Harry Brook’s batting here was more sensible and at a tempo in the captain’s mould. “He is still learning the art of Test cricket,” Root said. Thrusting Brook into the job would have put more pressure on him, he may well have felt he needed to make risky statements with the bat. Now he can mature under Root and Stephen Fleming.

Tactically, Root was astute and showed enough to suggest he is going to be different this time. The old Root would not have whipped Jofra Archer off after two overs of the Test, but it was a prod that worked as he bowled quicker and more accurately to strike twice with the second-innings new ball, using his new-found skills with a scrambled seam to good effect.

It also showed his bowlers he wanted a fuller length and, from that first hour, they controlled the match and did not let their grip slip.

Root promised to keep the good aspects of Bazball and apply common sense. He continued Stokes’s leg-slip tactic and it paid off with the wicket of opener Azan Awais, and urged Ollie Robinson to bowl with the keeper standing up. England batted at 4.5 an over – a touch quicker than the Bazball years – but it was never reckless, just a calm tempo, with no ramps or scoops.

News.title: Officials selling yellow fever certificates to unvaccinated travellers
News.content:
Officials in Malawi are selling yellow fever certificates to unvaccinated travellers for around $20 and sending them on their way, a Telegraph investigation has found.



The passport-sized, yellow document, officially called the International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP), is supposed to provide proof of vaccination against yellow fever, a mosquito-borne virus that kills tens of thousands of people every year.

The jab provides lifelong protection, beginning 10 days after vaccination. Most countries in Africa and Latin America require them for entry, either for all travellers or for those arriving from risk areas.



Yet travellers leaving Malawi through two major airports can get hold of the certificates without ever being vaccinated, according to interviews with multiple travellers and an undercover investigation.



Several passengers who travelled recently from Malawi to destinations including Uganda, Kenya, Ethiopia and China said they had obtained yellow fever vaccination certificates at airports or public hospitals without receiving the vaccine.



One traveller, who recently flew to Uganda for work from Kamuzu International Airport, which serves the capital, Lilongwe, said he was initially told it was too late to get vaccinated because his departure was less than 10 days away.



“When I asked the health officials if I could get vaccinated at the airport, I was told it was too late because I needed to be vaccinated ten days before my trip,” he told The Telegraph.



“But then they offered to arrange the certificate for me for roughly $21,” said the traveller, who asked not to be named. “I had to pay because I could not postpone the trip.”

News.title: Congo gambles on ‘old’ vaccine as new Ebola virus spirals
News.content:
Nearly half of all those infected have gone on to die.

Dr Sania Nishtar, chief executive of the Gavi global vaccine partnership, earlier this week said to beat the outbreak “we must deploy every tool at our disposal”.

She went on: “To avoid this becoming the worst recorded Ebola outbreak in history, it is critical that all effective countermeasure options are brought to bear.

“We have a tool that could help save lives while we wait for [Bundibugyo]-specific vaccines to become available.”

Previous clinical trials have shown that Ervebo is safe, but its effect on other strains is unknown.

The World Health Organisation said in a statement that while it was not known if Ervebo may protect against the Bundibugyo virus, “early laboratory and animal data suggest it may provide some protection”.

Medics told the Telegraph of anecdotal claims that health workers who had been given Ervebo to protect them during an outbreak of the Zaire strain in 2018 to 2020 had not fallen ill during the current Bundibugyo outbreak.

Health workers are at extreme risk of catching the disease because they come into contact with highly-contagious blood, vomit and diarrhoea from dying patients. When they fall sick themselves, they frequently go on to infect their own families.

Giving health workers vaccine jabs to protect them as they tend the sick is a cornerstone of Ebola responses.

The WHO said the vaccine allocation includes 20,000 doses for a Phase 3 clinical trial to understand the impact of the vaccine on the Bundibugyo virus. The remaining 50,000 doses will be used for front-line and health workers as recommended by WHO experts.

Dr Nishtar said: “Having already been licensed for the Zaire strain, we know that Ervebo is proven to be safe.

“And while the signs are that it may not stop transmission – which is essential for ending the outbreak - it could well save precious lives and reduce suffering.”

Health officials warn that the Bundibugyo outbreak centred on DRC’s Ituri province is easily outpacing relief efforts.

The virus is thought to have been spreading for months before an outbreak was finally declared in mid-May and medics have been unable to make up the head start.

An analysis by the Africa Centres for Disease Control meanwhile warned the current outbreak dwarfed all others on record

The current outbreak had almost ten times more cases than any other previous outbreak at a similar stage.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: Soaring welfare bill pushes national debt to almost £3tn
News.content:
Britain’s soaring welfare bill forced John Healey to borrow more to balance the books last month.

The gap between tax receipts and spending unexpectedly resulted in a £1.8bn deficit in July, taking the national debt to within a whisker of £3tn.

Economists had predicted the Government would borrow nothing and blamed the deficit on the rising welfare bill.

Figures published by the Office for National Statistics (ONS) this morning show total debt rose to £2.985tn in July.

Benefit payments also climbed by 7.2pc, or £2bn, to £30bn last month.

The Chancellor now faces another tax-raising Budget in October, even as strong receipts from self-employed workers provide some respite.

The ONS also said Mr Healey spent £7.7bn on debt interest in July alone, almost 10pc higher than a year ago.

Ashley Webb, at Capital Economics said: “The weak performance was mainly due higher social payments.”

Monthly borrowing was slightly higher than the Office for Budget Responsibility and markets expected, meaning the Government has borrowed £56.7bn this financial year to plug the gap between tax receipts and public spending.

Julian Jessop, an independent economist and IEA economics fellow, said: “The latest official data highlight the fragility of the public finances as John Healey prepares his first Budget. Government borrowing was £2.3bn above forecast in July, and £0.7bn higher than in the same month a year ago.”

July is traditionally a strong month for receipts from the self-employed, with self-assessed income tax receipts last month coming to £17.1bn, about £1.7bn more than a year earlier.

However, higher inflation triggered by the Iran war means Mr Healey will be forced to use the Budget to find billions of pounds to repair the public finances.

Mr Healey said: “Fiscal discipline is the bedrock of our UK economic stability and national security which is why we are committed to meeting our fiscal rules, with a buffer against global uncertainties.”

The Resolution Foundation warned that the Chancellor’s headroom against his fiscal rules - self-imposed guardrails to guide public spending - has shrunk from around £24bn in the Spring Statement to less than £8bn today.

The think tank called on the Chancellor to use his first Budget on Oct 28 to put the nation’s finances on a more sustainable path.

Elliott Christensen, senior economist at the Resolution Foundation, said: “The Chancellor’s margin against his fiscal rules is now razor thin.”

News.title: Brook falls agonisingly short of Headingley hundred again as England continue to dominate
News.content:
“Yeah, of course I did,” said Cox, when asked if he was frustrated to miss out on three figures. Cox was caught behind off spinner Ali Usman, but believed he had hit his pad with his bat, not the ball.

“Once I got to fifty, I moved to sixty quickly, and thought ‘there’s a chance here’. Just keep being disciplined, ball by ball. I had it at the back of my mind, thinking you have worked so hard, do not give this opportunity up. That is exactly what I do in county cricket. I get to fifty, see how many runs I need to score, and work down from there.”

Asked if his team-mates were feeling the same emotion, he said: “Oh yeah there is. Every team, every player wants to score Test hundreds. Four of us got fifties, so we were hoping one would kick on, and instead of making it just a hundred, make it 150 or 170.

“I am thrilled. I would have taken it at the start of the Test match. I let myself down a tiny bit, but at the end of the day, you take 70.”

Cox resumed on day two on 23, then was dropped by the bowler Khurram Shahzad on 57. In the course of his innings, he was compared to AB de Villiers by the former England captain Michael Vaughan.

Cox is likely to get a good run across formats. England had hoped to call on Sam Curran for the third Test of this series, but his summer is over due to a groin injury. Curran will undergo surgery on Friday.

It is likely England will be without Curran, Bethell and Tom Banton for September’s white-ball series against Sri Lanka, which should mean greater opportunity for the likes of Cox and Sussex’s James Coles, and could even see a recall for Zak Crawley, who made an assured 81 for Kent against Middlesex on Thursday. Will Jacks is currently sidelined with appendicitis, but is expected to have recovered in time for the series.

News.title: Robinson demolishes Pakistan to cement importance to new regime
News.content:
He also has that edge, the grunt of an angry fast bowler, and his competitiveness was just what Root needed considering his other quicks were still in Hundred mode. Archer bowled too short, Gus Atkinson grew into the innings but was wicketless and it took a while for Tongue to click, although once he did he was unplayable against the right-handers with his pace and angle.

Robinson’s lack of pace gives them the keeper-standing-up option. It worked a treat when he bowled Pakistan’s top-scorer, Abdullah Shafique for 61, his footwork messed up by Jamie Smith breathing down his neck.

Pakistan would have batted first had they won the toss and it is a good pitch that will improve as the Test goes on, although with rain around all week the overheads will have a say on the game. Pakistan have far more recent red-ball exposure than England’s batsmen but they were ill-equipped to deal with Robinson and Tongue.

Most supporters were still walking into the ground when the former struck first ball, Azan Awais lbw to a nip-backer. Shan Masood’s stilted footwork was ripe for exposing and Robinson’s first ball over the wicket to the left-hander was full and straight to beat the loose drive.

Imam-ul-Haq had done the hard work, seeing off Robinson only to flash a drive to second slip off a wide ball from Tongue to end Pakistan’s only stand of substance of the innings: 93 for the third wicket.

Robinson cracked the innings open further with Saud Shakeel leg before, who was too slow to call for the review that would have saved him. Hawk-Eye showed the ball would have gone over the top.

Robinson then bowled Shafique in his next over and Pakistan were toppling. Tongue cranked up the pace, bowled full and the perpendicular angle into the right-handers did the rest.

Sports.title: Strasbourg ‘in TRIPLE raid on Chelsea with Dario Essugo, Deivid Washington and Omari Kellyman set to join sister side’
Sports.content:
STRASBOURG are set to raid sister club Chelsea for three additions to their first team.

The French outfit are owned by the Todd Boehly-fronted BlueCo consortium, who also back Chelsea.



Transfer business between the pair has been prolific in recent years, and that trend shows no signs of slowing down as they look to complete a swoop for three Blues stars.

Deivid Washington is the first of the trio set to make the switch, with the Brazilian forward lined up for a permanent move to the Ligue 1 side.



Washington has found goals hard to come by since arriving as a teenager from Santos – where he was loaned back in 2025.

With the arrival of Emanuel Emegha from Strasbourg, Danny Welbeck‘s signing and the extension of Joao Pedro‘s contract, Washington’s chances of getting significant game time are much higher across the channel.

And he could be joined soon after by fellow forward Omari Kellyman, with the 20-year-old Englishman also set to follow on a permanent transfer, per L’Equipe.

They claim the former Aston Villa prospect will join on a deal which includes a buy-back clause.

And further still, youngster Dario Essugo, who signed from Sporting for almost £19million last summer, could be next in line for a stint in France.

The 21-year-old is a loan target for the club, who are looking to shore up their central midfield options.

The three signings would take the total number of moves from Chelsea to Strasbourg this window to five.

Goalkeeper Filip Jorgensen and defender Genesis Antwi both arrived on loan deals earlier in the window.

Meanwhile goalkeeper Mike Penders, defender Aaron Anselmino and forward David Datro Fofana have all returned from Strasbourg loans.

And with them they have brought Emegha and Valentin Barco on permanent moves to Stamford Bridge.

Sports.title: Ex-Arsenal star Jack Wilshere keeps bed in his Luton office and relies on power naps to cope with 24/7 management graft
Sports.content:
JACK WILSHERE has a BED in his office — because life in the dugout never stops.

Having played at the highest level for Arsenal and England, the ex-midfielder thought he knew true fatigue.



Taking charge at Kenilworth Road last October, Wilshere quickly realised playing is instinct, coaching is 24-hour graft.

The 34-year-old Hatters chief relies on 20-minute post-lunch power naps in his office to reset his brain.



And that relentless work ethic paid immediate dividends in Luton’s opening match of the season against Reading.

Trailing 3-1 at half-time, Wilshere delivered a rousing team talk that saw his side mount a brilliant second-half comeback to win 4-3.

Wilshere said: “It’s important to get a siesta when you can because coaching consumes your whole day.

“As a player, you train and go home. As a coach, you’re literally 24/7 on your laptop looking at clips, medical science, scouting and tactics. It never stops.”

That dedication brought Vertu Trophy glory in April — a special moment for a manager who first walked through the door as an eight-year-old academy kid.

Despite that Wembley triumph, missing out on the League One play-offs by a single point cut deep.

Wilshere is desperate to fire his boyhood club back towards the Premier League. But whether he is in a training tracksuit on the grass or a sharp suit on matchday, image matters.

Wilshere said: “There needs to be a balance. A manager should look important and command respect for the club, but you don’t want to be stuffy at the same time.

“You must be comfortable in your tracksuit gear when you’re out on the grass — and then differentiate yourself from the coaching staff on matchdays by being smart, casual.

“I wore a suit at Wembley because that’s a respect thing for me.

“You see guys like Gareth Ainsworth at Gillingham on the touchline looking like the front man in a rock band wearing jeans and a leather jacket!



“I don’t mind that because everyone’s got their own brand, but in this job, you simply can’t fake it.”

For Wilshere, there are no touchline ego trips, he is still “Jack from down the road” returning to his roots.

The Hatters boss said: “This club means a lot to me. The people here are honest, hard-working, and see right through anyone trying to play a character.



“You can’t come in here with an ego. You have to be yourself.”

That same drive for realness is why Wilshere cuts straight through the noise with today’s teenage prospects.

The former Gunners hero once dominated against a Barcelona midfield aged 19.

But he compares managing modern starlets to raising his own 14-year-old son in an instant-gratification world.

Wilshere said: “The language and culture are completely different now. Lads at 14 or 15 are dealing with TikTok, social media and massive hype.



“They want things really quickly. They want it now.

“When I was younger, you’d go and ask your mum and it would be, ‘Yeah, we’ll go to the shops at the weekend’ — or ‘No, you’re not getting it.’

“Whereas now, it’s ‘We can get it on Amazon’ and it arrives the same day. And that is kind of the mentality of footballers today.



“So a big part of my job is convincing players to believe in and commit to the process — and enjoy it.”

For Wilshere, real development takes time and making mistakes is vital.

He said: “If a player wants to improve their weak foot, they’re not going to go out tomorrow and practice it and be better at it.

“It’s going to take time. And experiencing things — sometimes that’s failure for a player — is better than me explaining it to them because they feel it, then they live it.

“A big thing is convincing the players to experience it, and that it’s okay to fail.”



The Hatters boss insists old-school hairdryer tactics instantly alienate footballers.

It is a far cry from only 15 years ago when Wilshere was a young player.

He said: “They see through it instantly. If you aren’t authentic, you lose the dressing room before you’ve even started. You simply can’t talk to them with bullst.”

To forge his style, Wilshere draws on two contrasting Arsenal legends who shaped his career.



He learned tactical obsession and relentlessness from Mikel Arteta while coaching at London Colney — and Arsene Wenger taught him the power of trust and human psychology as a player.

Wilshere said: “Learning from Mikel, seeing how detailed he is, it sets the standard.

“Every single second on the pitch matters. Being an Arsenal boy, you feel that identity deep inside.

“Arsene was incredible at making you feel invincible. He gave you total freedom and trust on the pitch, and that stays with you forever as a player and now as a coach.”

Wilshere is relishing locking horns this season with former Gunners team-mate Aaron Ramsey, who took charge at League One rivals Oxford.



The pair face off at Kenilworth Road in November before the February return at the MGroup Stadium.

He said: “We’ve had some banter about it already.

“It will be strange seeing each other in opposition dugouts after everything we shared together at Arsenal, but we’re both loving this next chapter.”

Wilshere keeps a close eye on the rising wave of young English managers fighting across the divisions.

And he said: “Look at guys like Michael Carrick, Frank Lampard, Gary O’Neil and Tom Cleverley.



“They’re forging a real path for young coaches. But you must produce straight away now. If you don’t get results, you’re out.”

Even as football falls in love with data analytics and algorithms, Wilshere stays grounded in basic human values.

He said: “Technology and data are evolving and AI is everywhere now.

“But AI can’t replace looking a player in the eye. It can’t replace heart.”

JACK WILSHERE'S DAILY ROUTINE JACK WILSHERE talks SunSport readers through a day in his life at manager of Luton Town — from his early alarm call to chilling at home in front of the TV at night. 5am EARLY ALARM My alarm goes off. I’ve got a six-year-old boy in a bad habit of climbing into our bed. So I’m normally stuck under him somewhere!

The habit of getting up so early is one I’ve dragged myself into. As a coach, if you don’t get ahead of your day before everyone else wakes up, you’re instantly playing catch-up. I get straight up and brush my teeth. I don’t shower because I’ve had one the night before. 5:10am DOG WALKING I’ve got two German Shepherds that need a bit of care so take them out, give them a drink and stuff before making myself a coffee for drive in 5:45pm DRIVING INTO TRAINING I get into the car and get talkSPORT on. I listen to the national football debate. I want to get myself into the mood and like to know what’s going on. 6:15am ARRIVE AT TRAINING GROUND I get into work and open up my computer. I’ve got a notebook sort of thing where I will write down what I need to do during the day. — and what I want other people in my staff to do too. 7:30am FIRST MEETING I’ll have my first meeting with the analysts, who arrive, and we’ll spend 45 minutes planning what we’re going to show the players on the screens in the morning. 8:30am STAFF MEETING All the medical, performance and coaching staff arrive and we meet up to discuss everything we need for the day. We’ll plan training and what the players are doing as well as map out our day. 9am BREAKFAST The chefs here are exceptional here. It varies day to day but they have a live food station and will rustle you up an ommlette or a protein bagel. 10am TEAM MEETING & PREP We’ll get the players together and talk through everything for about 20 minutes before they go off and start prepping. 11am TRAINING We’ll be doing that for an hour or an hour and half. Out on the grass, I’m hands-on, high-energy, setting standards, and pushing our tactical identity. 1pm LUNCH & POWER NAP After training, I’ll grab lunch and then a quick twenty-minute power nap. Coaching consumes your whole day. After debriefing and lunch, my brain is fried. A quick 20-minute shut-eye in the office completely resets my energy for an intense afternoon. 2pm CLIP ANALYSIS & SCOUTING Afternoons are for deep analysis: breaking down team sessions, prepping opposition video, checking youth prospects, or reviewing potential transfer targets. It’s relentless. 6:30pm DRIVE HOME All depends on the day but I drive home anytime between 5pm-7pm. 7PM — FAMILY TIME You’ve got to find ways to turn off. Evenings are for family. We’ll eat, hang out, and binge a TV series like Suits—the best way to get your mind completely off football. 10:30pm LIGHTS OUT I’m usually off to sleep around 10:30. I even track my sleep recovery stats now! I make sure I get enough rest before doing the whole crazy routine again the next day.

Sports.title: Why is Bruno Guimaraes not playing for Arsenal vs Coventry in Premier League opening game?
Sports.content:
ARSENAL host Coventry in the opening game of the new Premier League season tonight – but summer signing Bruno Guimaraes will not feature for the Gunners.

The former Newcastle captain signed a four-year deal at the Emirates in a deal worth £75million.



ARSENAL VS COVENTRY: LIVE COVERAGE

Arsenal are beginning the defence of their Premier League title tonight after beating out Manchester City last season.



They are also looking to go one step further in the Champions League after losing out on penalties in the final against PSG in May.

Since then, they have signed Greek winger Christos Tzolis, Guimaraes and agreed a deal for Aston Villa’s Ezri Konsa.

But only Tzolis is set to feature tonight with Konsa not yet announced at the Emirates and Guimaraes now unavailable.

Why isn’t Bruno Guimaraes playing for Arsenal vs Coventry?

Bruno Guimaraes has been ruled out of tonight’s clash after picking up an injury in his right thigh during the Community Shield against Manchester City last weekend.

The Brazilian played the first 45-minutes against Enzo Maresca‘s side, but was seen with ice on his leg during the second-half.

It didn’t stop the Gunners storming to a 3-0 win over their potential title rivals, but did cause fans some concern.



Mikel Arteta said in his press conference yesterday that he is “evolving really well, but let’s wait until tomorrow.”

However, Guimaraes has not recovered enough in time to feature in Arsenal‘s first game.

It is unclear how long he will be unavailable for at the moment.

Sports.title: Stoke keeper Viktor Johansson targets Premier League & promises fans the drinks are on him if they conquer Championship
Sports.content:
VIKTOR JOHANSSON is hoping the beers will be on him come May as he sets his sights on a dream Premier League promotion.

The Stoke keeper famously bought SIX HUNDRED pints for Rotherham supporters at the Cutlers Arms two years ago to thank them for standing by him through tough times before his move to the Potteries.





And if the 27-year-old Swedish international gets his way, Stoke supporters could be getting an even bigger rounds-on-me moment if he can help them conquer the Championship.

He told SunSport: “It was a famous story! I came in as a young goalkeeper and I had no expectations. I made loads of mistakes early on — but they were always behind me.



“They never had a bad word to say about me. They were always supportive, so here I am today. I can’t speak highly enough of them.

“Even when we were struggling, they made me their favourite and I won Player of the Year. I was so popular there. My motto is to treat people the way you want to be treated.



“If I can make people smile and put a smile on their faces, then I’m happy to help. It’s about being selfless — doing autographs, signing shirts. It doesn’t cost anything, does it?

“My granddad always taught me that, and my wife joins in too. It’s just about making people happy.”

That humility has instantly endeared him to the Stoke faithful, who are desperate to see their club end their Championship exile and return to the big time.

The Potteries has been starved of top-flight football for eight years but Johansson insists there is genuine belief in the dressing room that they can launch a promotion charge despite last weekend’s opening-day 2-1 loss against Swansea.

Ahead of this weekend’s trip to relegated Wolves, Johansson said: “I think we proved over a three or four-month spell last season that it could be us. There’s massive belief here. We just need to keep on going.

“Every team has a dip, but we need to make sure we climb that learning curve. Look at the teams coming down. West Ham are a big club in this division and Southampton didn’t go up last time.

“It’s a tough league, but we know what we are capable of achieving if we stay consistent.”

While many modern players complain about the relentless grind of a 46-game league campaign, the Swede thrives on the chaotic nature of the English second tier.

Between domestic cup ties and his growing international commitments, Johansson rarely gets a breathing space — and that is exactly how he likes it.



The 12-times capped Swedem keeper added: “I love it, yeah! It’s what I want to do as a footballer — play games. And when they come quick and fast, it’s even more enjoyable.

“People say there are too many games but I just love being out there. Coming from Sweden, making that leap, it’s just been constant. It’s been a big change but it suits me down to the ground. I enjoy the battle.”

That willingness to throw himself into the firing line stems from a fundamental truth about goalkeeping: it takes a unique mindset to stand between the sticks.



Johansson places shot-stoppers in a completely separate category to outfield players, acknowledging that the mental resilience required is off the charts.

He explained: “Goalkeepers are a different breed! We are in a separate category altogether — we’re our own union.

“Out on the pitch, if an outfield player makes a mistake, there’s usually someone behind them to cover. But when you’re in goal, you’re on your own.



“You’ve got to be thick-skinned. You’ve got to be a bit sharper upstairs and be ready for relentless pressure.”

That mental toughness was forged early in his career, including a memorable moment under legendary manager Neil Warnock at Sheffield United that left a lasting impression.

Recalling a raw moment early in his journey at Bramall Lane, Johansson revealed how Warnock protected him when he was at his lowest.

Johansson revealed: “I remember playing at against Sheffield United. I made a mistake, conceded a goal and I walked into the dressing room upset.

“I felt like I’d lost a million dollars. I was sitting there as a 19 or 20-year-old kid, devastated.

“Warnock walked in, saw the look on my face and just put his arms around me. He was absolute class. He protected me, uplifted me and made sure I didn’t dwell on it.

“He’s a proper football man, tough as old boots, but if you put a shift in for him, he’s in your corner all day long. He knows how to treat people and make them smile.”

Sports.title: Lionel Messi’s shirt he gave to Man Utd masseur sells for SIX TIMES what Cristiano Ronaldo’s went for in same auction
Sports.content:
A LIONEL MESSI shirt he gave to a Manchester United masseur at the peak of his powers has sold for SIX TIMES as much as a Cristiano Ronaldo one in the same auction.

Former Red Devils masseur Rod Thornley has been selling off his incredible collection of football shirts, which included a stunning collection of shirts from the iconic Class of ’92.



But his memorabilia set of kits does not end there, with one shirt from the best footballer of all time included.

Back in 2012, Man Utd played against Messi-led Barcelona in a pre-season friendly.



And a text sent to former defender Gerard Pique days before the game helped Thornley to secure one of the most-coveted shirts in football history.

Speaking to MatchWornShirt, Thornley revealed: “I messaged Gerard Piqué a couple of days before the game and said, I never ask you for anything, but I need Messi’s shirt from this one.

“At the end of the game Gerard came into our dressing room, grabbed me, and walked me straight into theirs.

“Messi still had the shirt on his back.

“He took it off, signed it to me while I sat there with him, and shook my hand. It was incredible.”

A staggering 14 years later, the shirt has now been sold at auction for a huge sum as part of MatchWornShirt’s Legends Collection.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho admits Jude Bellingham, Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Jr may not play together in ‘difficult’ Real Madrid XI
Sports.content:
REAL MADRID boss Jose Mourinho has admitted it will be “difficult” for his superstar trio of Jude Bellingham, Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius to play together.

Mourinho, 63, has returned to the Bernabeu 13 years after his last stint came to an end.



The former Chelsea boss has inherited a talented side that has under-performed despite boasting big name stars like Mbappe, Vinicius and Bellingham.

Madrid had a rare trophyless season in 2025-26 and only won the Uefa Super Cup in the previous campaign.



And Mourinho says he faces a dilemma to find the right system that is “perfect” for the three of them.

He told the media: “They are incredible players and incredible players want to play with incredible players.



“Top players have frustration when they play with teammates who are not top.

“The best want to play with the best. After the tactical adjustments, it might be a little bit more difficult.

[Carlo] Ancelotti has found the perfect Brazil for Vini, [Didier] Deschamps for Kylian in France, [Thomas] Tuchel for Jude.

“It is more difficult for Mourinho to find a team that’s perfect for the three of them. But there we are. I want the three to feel comfortable on the field when they play.

Sports.title: Hull star Matt Crooks set for Premier League debut against boyhood club Man United 18 years after heart-breaking release
Sports.content:
MATT CROOKS remembers arriving at Carrington as an eight-year-old kid — and crossing paths with Rio Ferdinand the day he signed for Manchester United.

Six years later the lifelong fan was in tears after being axed by the Red Devils.



Now, after rebuilding his career from the depths of non-league, the Hull star is ready to face his childhood club as he made his Premier League debut aged 32..

The Tigers host United at the MKM Stadium on Saturday in their first top-flight game for nine years after winning the Championship play-off final against Middlesbrough in May.



And for Crooks, walking out against United completes a wild 18-year journey.

The midfielder told SunSport: “I went to Carrington to pick up some boots and kit and it just happened to be the day Rio Ferdinand was signing for United from Leeds.



“He was walking down the steps in a white suit. My dad and grandad — who are both massive United fans — were there with me and it was a pretty surreal moment.

“That’s one of the main memories that sticks with me.

“I joined United when I was an eight and got released at 14. I thoroughly enjoyed my time there. There were loads of great people and fantastic opportunities.

“Looking back, you probably don’t realise at the time just how lucky you are, the things you get to experience, and the chances you’re given.”

Being shown the door by the Premier League giants as a youngster proved to be a crushing blow.

Crooks was forced to rebuild his life and career, dropping into non-league on loan at Halifax Town and Radcliffe Borough before embarking on an extensive EFL journey with Hartlepool, Scunthorpe, Northampton, Rotherham and Middlesbrough.

He even sampled football with Rangers in Scotland and Real Salt Lake in MLS before helping Hull seal their top-flight return.

Crooks added: “I remember crying when they told me they were letting me go.

“I went to the Trafford Centre with my dad afterwards for some food. And he was saying, ‘Listen, what do you want? Do you want to work even harder or do you want to call it a day?’



“I think my dad embedded that in me. I’m lucky to have good support around me family-wise.

“I always said I probably wasn’t good enough technically on the ball, so I had to go elsewhere. It’s part and parcel of academy football and the system that’s been created within that.

“It was the first time I had a fork in the road. I had to decide if I’d carry on playing football or just give up.



“That was the time I learned about myself a little bit and had the confidence to go again, start afresh and try to prove some people wrong. Rejection definitely shapes you.”

This will not be the first time Crooks has targeted an upset against his boyhood club.

Four years ago, while with Boro, he scored an equaliser at Old Trafford in an FA Cup fourth-round tie before his side stunned United 8-7 on penalties.

Crooks said: “To go to Old Trafford and play against them was surreal.

“For a certain point in your career, you wonder if you’re ever going to be capable of stepping foot on a Premier League pitch.



“We knocked them out and to have my family and friends in the crowd was so cool, so special.

“This weekend will be a huge challenge. The quality in their squad is ridiculously high — the speed, the athleticism, every single player is a powerful, big guy.

“You have to look at yourself as a group and realise we’ve earned the right to be here. You aren’t put in this position if you aren’t good enough.

“So to make my debut against Man United, it’s going to be a really proud moment.”

Hull have splashed the cash in an ambitious transfer window, headlined by big-money moves for centre-back Nobel Mendy (Rayo Vallecano, £20m), keeper Konstantinos Tzolakis (Olympiacos, £20m) and centre-back Lucas Herrington (Colorado, £12.7m).



The recruitment spree continues right across the pitch, with central midfielders Jens Hjertø-Dahl (Tromsø IL) and Hidemasa Morita (Sporting) arriving alongside defensive midfielders Lucas Gourna-Douath (Salzburg) and Óscar Zambrano (NK Maribor).

They have also strengthened in attack with centre-forward Joe Gelhardt (Leeds) and left midfielder Elliot Stroud (Mjällby AIF), while adding further defensive depth in left-back Matt Targett (Newcastle) and keeper Jack Butland (Rangers).

Hull secured their top-flight return in breathless fashion at Wembley with Ollie McBurnie netting a late winner.

And Crooks admits the dressing room is buzzing off the energy brought in by their new-look squad under manager Sergej Jakirovic.

Crooks said: “Wembley was a complete blur. Ollie scoring that late winner and the scenes that followed, the celebrations… it was brilliant.



“We’ve brought in some top lads and everyone has been chumming together already.

“We’ve got five or six guys in competitive positions now, so hopefully that drives up the quality and helps us in that regard with strength in the dressing room.

“The gaffer deserves massive credit for the job he’s done. He’s jovial, funny, always having a laugh, but when it’s time to be serious, he’s the gaffer.

“He is very direct — there’s no b***s*** with him.

“The manager has huge ambition and the message to us for this campaign has been crystal clear.

“The chairman travels 18 hours to watch us, so we don’t want to be distracted.

“We haven’t come up with a mindset just to survive or be distracted by the naysayers. We want to keep pushing, be successful, and show everyone we belong here.”

Sports.title: Chelsea REJECT Leeds bid for Mykhailo Mudryk with Brentford and Coventry also keen on loan transfer
Sports.content:
LEEDS UNITED have had a bid rejected by Chelsea to take Mykhailo Mudryk on loan in a three way Premier League battle for the Ukrainian winger.

Leeds, managed by Daniel Farke, are joined by Frank Lampard‘s Coventry in being keen on having Mudryk in their ranks, while Brentford previously showed an interest in him too.



Leeds’ first offer fell short of Chelsea‘s expectations, with the club exploring multiple options from within the Premier League and abroad, with Mudryk himself happy to spend the season on loan to rebuild his fitness.

One of those abroad options is spending the season at sister club RC Strasbourg.



Dream Team is back, free, and there’s £100,000 up for grabs!

But if he is to do that, he will take up the last available loan spot, which is likely to be kept open until the end of the window should BlueCo need it.

That spot in north-eastern France could also be taken up by Dario Essugo, who is also looking for regular minutes away from Stamford Bridge after only making six appearances as he needed surgery on a quadriceps injury last season.



A source told SunSport that Brentford’s attraction to Mudryk extends back to when he was at Shakhtar, but when he started performing in the Champions League his value exceeded what the side were willing to pay.

But now, having returned from his suspension, they are showing interest again.

The problem with a move to Brentford is that the Bees would like to take him permanently rather than on loan.

There is also a chance that Mudryk stays at Stamford Bridge, though it is considered unlikely.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Mudryk has not played a competitive match since the end of November 2024, when he featured for Chelsea in the Conference League in a 2-0 win against Heidenheim, in which he scored.

He was suspended after meldonium, a prohibited substance, was discovered in a sample provided while on international duty with Ukraine.

The winger was handed a four-year ban, which he has successfully appealed, and then he returned to Chelsea to join Xabi Alonso‘s side on pre-season tour in Hong Kong, making his return in a friendly against Juventus.

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: New Liverpool bid, Arsenal deal agreed, three Man Utd moves
Sports.content:
The latest transfer news and rumours from the Premier League and around the world as deadline day edges closer

Hello and welcome to Mirror Football's live transfer blog on Friday, August 20.

The big news on Thursday was that Liverpool had a £50m bid for Yankuba Minteh rejected by Brighton & Hove Albion. The Reds have been scouring the market for wingers this summer and tabled an opening offer for the Gambia international after shortlisting him earlier this year.

However, while the player is believed to be keen on a move to Anfield, Liverpool’s offer falls short of Brighton’s valuation, and it remains to be seen whether the Reds will return with another offer.

Curtis Jones, meanwhile, is set to complete a move to Inter Milan in a transfer that could be worth £30million. He has had permission to fly to Italy to undergo a medical after a deal was agreed on Thursday.

While Manchester City are pursuing a deal for Palmeiras winger Allan, as Savinho remains in talks with Tottenham Hotspur. But one man who won’t be leaving his club this summer is Myles Lewis-Skelly, as Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta yesterday ruled out a transfer happening this summer.

The Gunners also continue to be linked with a move for Julian Alvarez from Atletico Madrid, with one report claiming a deal between the Spanish club and the Gunners had been agreed. Alvarez, though, still favours a move to Barcelona.

And Manchester United have reportedly contacted Barcelona to ask about Alejandro Balde's situation at the club. The Red Devils are keen to add a left-back to the squad this summer, and it is claimed that Barca are willing to listen to offers for Balde this summer.

We will keep you up to date on those moves and much more right here on our blog below...

Sports.title: Chelsea secure agreement to host Champions League games for Shakhtar Donetsk
Sports.content:
Chelsea secure agreement to host Champions League games for Shakhtar Donetsk

Shakhtar Donetsk will play their home Champions League games at Stamford Bridge after striking a deal with Chelsea, who failed to qualify for Europe

View 2 Images Stamford Bridge will host Champions League football this season

Chelsea will host Champions League football this season after they agreed to let Shakhtar Donetsk play their home games at Stamford Bridge.

‌



The Ukrainian side have not played a match at their home stadium, the Donbas Arena, for more than 12 years due to the Russian invasion into Ukraine.

‌



As a result they've played across Europe with Shakhtar having to call the likes of Hamburg and Warsaw their temporary homes. Now they'll call London their home for a year and have settled on using Chelsea's ground having also considered playing at Brentford’s Gtech Stadium.

‌



Chelsea endured a poor year last season, going through two permanent managers, which meant they finished down in tenth and thus failed to qualify for any kind of European football.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

That has left Stamford Bridge free on Champions League nights and the Blues have decided to allow Shakhtar to play their home games in west London with the group stage draw still to be made.

‌



A Chelsea statement read: "FC Shakhtar have played in countries across Europe and we look forward to welcoming them to London for their Champions League campaign this year. We will be working with the Shakhtar team closely over the coming weeks to ensure that matchdays run safely and smoothly for their team and supporters."

Shakhtar have only played once at Stamford Bridge, that coming in November 2012 when they were undone by a last minute Victor Moses header in a five-goal thriller.

View 2 Images Shakhtar Donetsk's only outing at Stamford Bridge came back in 2012

‌



Shakhtar themselves have thanked the Premier League side for the opportunity. They said: "Playing our Champions League home matches at Stamford Bridge is a special opportunity for Shakhtar. We are grateful to Chelsea Football Club for the opportunity to host our games at this special venue. Stamford Bridge is one of the most famous stadiums in world football, with an incredible history and atmosphere. We are convinced that Shakhtar’s matches in London will provide unforgettable emotions for Ukrainian and English fans."

The Ukrainian side's best effort in the Champions League came back in 2011, when they made the quarter-finals. They topped a group that included Arsenal, beating the north Londoners at home, before Pep Guardiola's Barcelona ended their journey.

Sports.title: Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler responds to Man Utd's bid for Carlos Baleba
Sports.content:
Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler responds to Man Utd's bid for Carlos Baleba

Manchester United have submitted an offer of £60million plus £5m in add-ons for Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba, who will sit out of their Premier League opener this weekend

View 3 Images Fabian Hurzeler spoke about transfer rumours involving his players (Image: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler refused to be drawn on Manchester United's interest in midfielder Carlos Baleba on the eve of their Premier League campaign.

‌



United have submitted an offer of £60million plus £5m in add-ons for the 22-year-old, who Michael Carrick wants to further bolster his midfield alongside new arrivals Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos.

‌



Baleba is keen on a move to Old Trafford and has reportedly already agreed personal terms. United first enquired about the Cameroon international last summer and are now confident they can wrap up a deal for considerably less than the £100m they were quoted 12 months ago.

‌



Hurzeler faced reporters on Friday ahead of Brighton's Premier League opener against Aston Villa on Sunday and didn't give much away, bar confirming Baleba would miss the game due to an ankle injury picked up in pre-season.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"He's a Brighton player. Like I said, I'll never comment on any rumours that are currently in the media, it's also something I definitely can't control," the German said.

"A lot of things are written, I know about situations but again, in two days I have a very important game together with my team and with my staff. We want to have a good start in the Premier League season, that's the only focus we have at the moment."

His words echoed those of Brighton chief executive Paul Barber the day before. "It’s not something that I can talk about right now," Barber told talkSPORT on Thursday.

‌



View 3 Images Manchester United are confident of signing Carlos Baleba (Image: Getty Images)

"This time of year we’re always going to be subject to bids for our players, we’re always going to be interested in ones that are sensible and are going to make sense for us financially, economically. But we also have to balance that with making sure our squad is as strong as it can be to compete in competitions like the one we’re in.

"So nothing really to say on Carlos at the moment other than that he’s a hugely talented young midfielder who’s done really well for us and has attracted interest from some of the biggest clubs in the world now for a couple of years."

‌



Brighton are also fielding interest from Liverpool in winger Yankuba Minteh. The Seagulls have rejected a £50m bid from Andoni Iraola's side and know the transfer game better than most, having lost many key players to Premier League rivals in recent years.

View 3 Images Yankuba Minteh is wanted by Liverpool (Image: Crystal Pix/MB Media/Getty Images)

"We know in general all the players there are rumours about, they are important players for us because they're a big part of the journey the last two years," Hurzeler said.

‌



"In football, you have to understand, it's normal if you're successful as a team, if the team is doing well, they've had some good achievements, then an individual can shine. Then of course there will be a big ask for our players, that's part of our identity and part of my job here.

"It was clear for everyone this might happen during a busy transfer window. We can go through every individual player, we all know how important these kinds of players are for me, but we also know that good achievements, big achievements, especially in the Premier League, you create offers, you create a lot of attention."

Sports.title: Arsenal complete stunning Ezri Konsa deal with defender set for instant Aston Villa reunion
Sports.content:
Arsenal complete stunning Ezri Konsa deal with defender set for instant Aston Villa reunion

Arsenal have made their fifth permanent signing of the summer by welcoming Aston Villa and England defender Ezri Konsa to the Emirates Stadium in a £51m deal with their Premier League rivals

View 3 Images Ezri Konsa has joined Arsenal from Aston Villa (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Arsenal have completed the signing of Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa as the latest stage of their summer spending spree. The Gunners have aimed for a refresh of their squad this summer after lifting last season’s crown.

‌



The north London side have already completed five deals, with moves for Bruno Guimaraes, Christos Tzolis and Illan Meslier, while Piero Hincapie has also completed a permanent switch to the Emirates.

‌



Aston Villa and England star Konsa has now become the fifth addition of the summer window. Arsenal agreed to pay £51million for his services, with a further £4m in add-ons.

‌



Konsa, 28, has signed a four-year deal with his new employers and will now give Arsenal more defensive options, with William Saliba set for a spell on the sidelines with a back injury.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



“I’m super excited. It's a privilege to be here and can’t wait to get started,” Konsa said. “I want to keep winning, I’m hungry to win and that’s what I’m here for. It's a proud moment for me and my family to play for one of the best teams in the world.”

"We’re delighted to have completed the signing of Ezri Konsa," Arsenal sporting director Andrea Berta said.

“Ezri is a defender of high quality, whose athleticism, composure and tactical intelligence have established him as one of the Premier League’s most consistent performers. Being comfortable in both central defence and at right-back, Ezri will bring valuable versatility to our squad while maintaining the high defensive standards which are fundamental to our challenge of winning major trophies.

‌



“We are welcoming a player with proven Premier League and international experience, and strong leadership qualities, who will adapt seamlessly to our style of play. Just as importantly, we are welcoming a player with the character and mentality to make an immediate impact within our club."

View 3 Images Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta and sporting director Andrea Berta with Ezri Konsa (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Konsa leaves Villa after a hugely successful seven-year spell in the Midlands. He joined the side from Brentford in 2019 and went on to make 286 appearances for the club, helping them to the Europa League last term, as well as three seasons in Europe.

‌



He will quickly be reunited with his former club, with Arsenal taking on Emery's side next weekend in their second game of the campaign. Konsa’s arrival comes off the back of comments from Arsenal CEO Richard Garlick as he vowed that the club would only be signing players that took them to the next level this summer.

He said: "It's players that are going to take Arsenal forward. In the past we've looked at players that maybe helped build out the squad or get us to a certain level, but now we're competing right at the top level, and we do need to bring in players that are going to change the dial.

View 3 Images The Gunners have paid an initial £51m fee for Konsa (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"That might be younger players that come into your squad and give them time to develop, and you've seen that in the last couple of years at Arsenal, and if we're able to combine those players that are coming through the academy with some of the best players in the world then we've got every chance of maintaining that success and going beyond what we've already achieved."

He added: "We said at the start of this season we're about to embark on that we're not going to stand still and pat ourselves on the back and say, 'Well done, job done, nothing else to do'. We want to move forward - the best clubs are always moving forward.

"You can see we've already invested in the squad this season, and if the right opportunity arises, then we will look to strengthen in all areas."

Sports.title: VAR protest planned for this weekend as fans rebel against 'robbing the joy of football'
Sports.content:
VAR protest planned for this weekend as fans rebel against 'robbing the joy of football'

Fans groups have united to make their feelings on the technology clear

View 3 Images Many fans have had enough of VAR (Image: Harry Langer/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images)

German football fans are planning mass VAR protests this weekend after accusing the technology of "robbing the joy of football." The protest will coincide with the first round of the German Cup, which won't actually use VAR.

‌



Competition rules dictate that lower league sides, which cannot accommodate the system, must play at home. Protesting fans say it means they will "see football as it should: without VAR and, therefore, authentic, immediate and full of excitement."

‌



The ambition of the protest is to rid German football of VAR. A fans' group statement, titled "VAR is robbing us of the joy of football," said: "Instead of spontaneous joy after a goal, there are now doubts about a possible review. VAR has destroyed the most emotional moment of the game.

‌



"We want to return to that state permanently and are therefore calling for the abolition of Video Assistant Refereeing in German football."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The statement added: "While football thrives on intensity and rhythm, the flow of the game suffers significantly from protracted interruptions. We are also painfully aware that it has destroyed the game’s most emotional moments.

‌



Pro Ref implement Premier League crackdown on grappling as Howard Webb fires warning READ MORE :

"Even fans who were initially open to and positive about the innovation now acknowledge, after nine years, that VAR has fundamentally altered the character of the game."

Sadly for the protesting fans, VAR is set for an even bigger role in top-tier games this season. As seen at the World Cup, the system can now be deployed to assess second yellow cards that have been awarded. However, the technology won't be used for potential second bookings that haven't been shown.

View 3 Images VAR will have a greater say in decisions this season (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

‌



VAR will also be used to review whether a foul has been committed before the set-piece was taken. If a foul is spotted, the goal will be ruled out and the set-piece retaken.

It is unclear what form the protests will take but German fans have a track record for mobilising to challenge contentious issues in the game, like ticket prices, kick-off times and the deal between the Bundesliga and a private investment fund. Previous protests have seen tennis balls and chocolate coins thrown onto pitches.

View 3 Images German football fans aren't afraid to protest (Image: Leon Kuegeler/Getty Images)

Article continues below

While the majority of first round matches take place this weekend, starting on Friday, Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund won't play until next month as they face off in the German Super Cup on Saturday night. Bayern visit Osnabruck on September 2, while Dortmund travel to HEBC the day before.

Sports.title: Julian Alvarez to Arsenal twist as huge transfer agreement wrecks forward's dream move
Sports.content:
Julian Alvarez to Arsenal twist as huge transfer agreement wrecks forward's dream move

Barcelona are still trying to replace Robert Lewandowski this summer, and like Arsenal, the Catalan club are credited with a transfer interest in Julian Alvarez

View 2 Images Barcelona are apparently lining up alternatives to Julian Alvarez (Image: Europa Press Sports, Europa Press via Getty Images)

Lautaro Martinez is reportedly emerging as an alternative to Julian Alvarez for Barcelona. Atletico Madrid are apparently open to negotiating with Arsenal for the Argentina international.

‌



Alvarez, 26, is believed to have his heart set on signing for the Catalan club, despite his employers being unwilling to do business with them. Barcelona have yet to replace Robert Lewandowski during this summer transfer window and face the prospect of starting the La Liga season with Raphinha as their sole central striker.

‌



The Gunners, conversely, signed Viktor Gyokeres barely 12 months ago. However, they could end up swapping the Swede for Alvarez.

‌



El Chiringuito claim Barcelona's head coach, Hansi Flick, and sporting director, Deco, are extremely interested in securing Martinez. The latter is reported to have held discussions with their football co-ordinator, Bojan, and the Argentine's representative, Alejandro Camano, in Madrid last week.

The reporting suggests they have effectively already reached an agreement in principle with the player on personal terms. An initial proposal from Barcelona will apparently not exceed £86 million (€100m).

Yet, like Atletico, Inter are reluctant to part with their striker, who also captains the Milanese outfit. Gazzetta dello Sport emphasises that they are not considering his exit.

‌



View 2 Images Julian Alvarez is training with Atletico Madrid, but did not play in their La Liga opener against Malaga (Image: Europa Press Sports, Europa Press via Getty Images)

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Fans in Madrid are, meanwhile, making their displeasure towards Alvarez abundantly clear, with several banners appearing around the club's Sports City bearing the message "JULIAN OUT" alongside his shirt number 19 crossed out. Supporters voiced similar frustrations ahead of yesterday's La Liga curtain-raiser against Malaga.

‌



A banner unveiled earlier in the week read: "Julian, thank you for the respect you are having for us, a**hole. Barca and your circle have deceived you like a capricious child. Our Atleti above all."

Alvarez was absent from the matchday squad at Metropolitano Stadium last night. He has not featured for Atletico at all since last season.

The former Manchester City striker has his sights firmly set on Barcelona and appears to have no desire to return to the Premier League. Atletico are equally reluctant to do business with their domestic rivals, leaving the impasse very much intact.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola issues Liverpool transfer update as he teases multiple deals before deadline
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola issues Liverpool transfer update as he teases multiple deals before deadline

Liverpool go into the new Premier League campaign with a light squad following a raft of departures

View 2 Images Time is running out for Andoni Iraola to improve Liverpool's ranks this summer

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola failed to be drawn on summer transfer targets but hinted at multiple arrivals. The Reds have lost a number of experienced figures this summer with Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate leaving the club.

‌



Curtis Jones is set to leave his boyhood club as he formalises a permanent move to Inter Milan, ending a 20-year association with the club. Liverpool are interested in Paris Saint-Germain star Bradley Barcola, while they saw a bid for Yankuba Minteh rejected and are strongly linked with PSG's Ibrahim Mbaye.

‌



Iraola has been steadfast in his pursuit of reinforcements in the window and has hinted at potential additions. He said: "As a manager, this is an easy one for me. I wanted the players for the first day, July 13, everyone here all the positions covered, top level players.

‌



Jamie Carragher brands Florian Wirtz a £40m player in brutal warning to Liverpool star READ MORE :

Liverpool receive Brighton response after launching £50m Yankuba Minteh transfer bid READ MORE :

"You understand how the competition works, the market is open and you start the competition.

"We will have to adapt as coaches to this situation, there is a lot of uncertainty but everywhere while the market it open. Honestly I don't spend too much time thinking about these things.

"I know you will ask me a lot of questions but I am focused on the game at Newcastle, that is massive for me, and using the very good players we have right now in the building in the best way so we can be competitive from the beginning.

‌



"What do we need? There are certain situations we need, specifically in the wing, other positions we have to be open-minded in the market that can honestly improve our team. It's about improving the squad, we have very good players already, to improve we need specific players."

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Jones has been at a crossroads in his Liverpool career having failed to cement a regular starting berth on Merseyside. He was the subject of loan interest from Italy in the past but going into the final 12 months of his contract at Anfield, he is set to depart with the Reds on the verge of earning £30million for his sale.

‌



Iraola admitted that he wanted to keep the Englishman in the ranks, speaking highly of the Liverpool academy graduate. It leaves Liverpool light in midfield but opens the door to opportunities for James McConnell and Trey Nyoni, who have impressed in pre-season.

The Basque tactician admitted that they will keep an open-mind in the window regarding additions, specifically stating that there will be no slap-dash movement in the market.

View 2 Images Curtis Jones looks set to leave Liverpool for Inter Milan (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Iraola said: "We cannot speak about players that are not ours. I understand the questions. With Curtis, I think it is not still official but there is an ongoing situation.

"I spoke to him in the first or second training session, I value him a lot as a player and he loves this club. I understood the outcome was going to be what it has been at the end.

"In terms of you are asking me what we need, there are certain situations for me that are clear, especially on the wing as we don't have enough players specific to play in those positions. I think we have to be open and open minded in the market to situations that honestly can improve our team."

Sports.title: Brighton reject £60m Liverpool bid for Minteh
Sports.content:
Brighton have rejected a £60m bid from Liverpool for winger Yankuba Minteh.

Sky Sports News understands the proposal did not meet Brighton's valuation after the Reds previously failed with a £50m bid for the 22-year-old.

Minteh is currently unavailable due to an injury, which is likely to keep him out until October. Brighton are also without Kaoru Mitoma, who has been sidelined since May with a hamstring injury.

Brighton are also in talks with Manchester United over the sale of Carlos Baleba, with an agreement understood to be close over a deal worth in excess of £60m.

Liverpool prioritising reinforcements out wide

Reinforcing in wide-forward areas has been Liverpool's priority throughout this window after already signing Victor Munoz from Osasuna earlier in the window.

As part of Liverpool's process to add in wide areas, they are looking at a number of possibilities, one of those being Minteh.

Liverpool have been pursuing Bradley Barcola at Paris Saint-Germain and remain in contact with the European champions over a deal.

However, PSG's £145m valuation is a complicating factor as Liverpool do not currently want to reach that figure.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Transfer Talk podcast panel discuss Bradley Barcola's potential move to Liverpool and whether or not the French forward would live up to the big money expectations.

Hurzeler: It's normal to have players linked with moves

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler says it is normal for players to be linked away with moves given the success of the Seagulls across recent season.

Minteh and Baleba are the latest Brighton players to attract transfer interest, after already losing Jan Paul van Hecke to Tottenham and Danny Welbeck to Chelsea earlier in the window.

Speaking ahead of their season opener against Aston Villa on Sunday, live on Sky Sports, Hurzeler said: "We know in general, all the players who there are rumours about are important players, they've been part of the journey over the last two years.

"It's normal that if a team is doing well, then there will be a big ask for players. That's part of my job here, it's part of our identity.

"We can go through every individual player, we know how important they are but we know good achievements, big achievements, you create a lot of attention and therefore we have to wait now.

"The situation will evolve. I'm not here to complain, I'm here to find solutions."

Sports.title: Kevin Blake's York tips: Ebor Festival day four picks
Sports.content:
Sky Sports Racing's Kevin Blake reveals a trio of picks as York's Ebor Festival concludes with yet another wildly-competitive card on day four on Saturday.

York have been unlucky with the weather this week, and the softening ground has created some extra challenges, but all being well we can hopefully finish the week on a high.

The Sky Bet Strensall Stakes (1:50) is the first race of interest, and one that looks overpriced is the Hamad Al Jehani-trained Archivist. Long-term readers may recall that I put him up as my selection in the Royal Hunt Cup at Royal Ascot and while it didn't work out for him on the day, he gained compensation on his very next start when overcoming what was considered a near impossible draw of 20 in the Golden Mile at Glorious Goodwood.

Not only did he overcome his draw, he did it with a bit to spare and that performance signalled his readiness to be competitive at stakes level. This course and distance should suit him well and any ease in the ground shouldn't be overly inconvenient for him. He is drawn a little wider than ideal, but that is bearable given his price is so big. A big run from him wouldn't at all surprise.

The Sky Bet Constantine Handicap (4:10) is another extremely tough sprint handicap, but I'm game to have a swing at the Andrew Balding-trained Dance In The Storm. The manner in which the betting markets have been so positive about her in her four starts this season has strongly suggested that she is considered better than a handicapper.

While she has won two of her four starts over seven furlongs this season, she has very much been shaping as though she is worth a try at this shorter trip. She has a career-high mark to overcome, but this different distance could well unlock notable further improvement. She is a really interesting contender and warrants support.

The final selection of the week comes in the concluding Sky Bet Dav Reid Finale Handicap (5:20), and it is the Ger Lyons-trained Diego El Queso. The four-year-old has a progressive profile, winning a handicap at Leopardstown in good style back in April prior to having an absence of 12 weeks that suggests he may have had a hold up.

He returned to action with a tremendous run to finish second to Thread Of Gold in a valuable handicap back at Leopardstown and that form has been well advertised by the winner since then. He was well fancied for a similar race to this at Glorious Goodwood, but the race went wrong for him, yet he still managed to catch the eye in finishing sixth.

He is capable of better than he was able to show there and with both this course and distance and the ease in the ground all promising to suit him, he can be expected to make a bold bid for compensation.
